findings.passage: Repeal the Second Amendment: The second amendment has been grossly corrupted, transforming it from an 18th century militia regulation provision to the modern-day right to own weapons of war. We should repeal it and empower all levels of government to impose reasonable gun safety laws without constitutional threat.
findings.note: Campaign issue page (undated; page is from the 2026 congressional campaign) calls for repealing the Second Amendment.

findings.passage: Every gun sale — whether at a store, a gun show, or online — should require a background check.
findings.note: Campaign issue page, under the heading Universal Background Checks, says every sale needs a check.

findings.passage: We need to restore the federal ban on military-style assault weapons and limit the high-capacity magazines that turn mass shootings into massacres.
findings.note: Campaign issue page, under the heading Assault Weapons Ban, supports a federal ban and magazine limits.

findings.passage: We can save lives by temporarily removing guns from people who pose a danger to themselves or others. Red flag laws work — when we actually use them.
findings.note: Campaign issue page, under the heading Red Flag Laws.

findings.passage: Too many children die from accidental shootings at home. Responsible gun ownership means safe storage. We passed safe storage requirements in Evanston and we should do it nationwide.
findings.note: Campaign issue page, under the heading Safe Storage Requirements; calls for national safe storage rules.

findings.passage: The gun industry is the only industry in America with broad legal immunity. That must end. Victims of gun violence deserve their day in court.
findings.note: Campaign issue page, under the heading Ending Gun Industry Immunity.

findings.passage: Biss said the bill would work to prevent people who do not possess a license issued by the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation from purchasing firearms.
findings.note: Daily Northwestern reports, in its own words, that as a state senator he backed a gun dealer licensing bill he planned to introduce; this is the paper's description of his statement, not a direct quote. Bill number not found.
subjects: limits on who may sell or buy guns

findings.passage: It shouldn’t take another Sandy Hook, Columbine, Orlando, or Las Vegas to call this problem what it is: a public health crisis.
findings.note: Direct quote of him, as quoted by the Daily Northwestern, in a statement after the Las Vegas shooting.
